title: Python: the bound or constraint of a type alias in a class body is read eagerly through an enclosing or module binding, not the class's final binding: wrong edge on dev (DEC-303 (a74) item 3)
description: HOLD, wrong edge on dev. Filed record-only under DEC-303 (a74) item 3, found while running (a74)'s bounds experiment for GCLI-144's round 1 (opum-ai/glyph-cli#223). The bound or constraint of a type alias is walked (the alias case pushes its left side, type parameters included, in the enclosing scope), so a call inside it is a recorded site, but it resolves as an EAGER class-body read. Python evaluates an alias bound lazily in the alias's annotation scope, which sees the class's FINAL bindings, so a name the class body binds by a LATER import is that import, never an enclosing or module binding. MEASURED on origin/dev 4e186bfb (identical on the GCLI-144 head; not a regression), source = class C with def run; x = C() at module level or in def outer(); class Outer: type A[T: x.run()] = int; then from m import X as x (m.X has run): alias bound gives calls 2, edges [C, C.run] (WRONG: x is the later import m.X at evaluation time); the same with x = C() in def outer(): edges [C, C.run]; constraint tuple type A[T: (x.run(), int)] = int: [C, C.run]; control type A[T] = x.run() (the value, refused by GCLI-144's lazy guard): the value case is fixed there, the bound is not. Twins on dev: def f[T: x.run()](self) in the class body and class K[T: x.run()] record only the x = C() call, no edge, because def and class bounds are not walked (GCLI-145, ordinary). Module-level type A[T: x.run()] = int with a single module x = C() gives C.run, correct there. RULE (the same invariant as GCLI-144, DEC-303 (a73)/(a74) item 2, for the alias bound): a read inside the bound of a class-body alias is a lazy read; it is refused when Rule 38 dropped a binding of the name, and otherwise keeps its edge; it should only REMOVE edges. Walk the bound in the alias's lazy type-parameter scope (Scope.lazyAlias, GCLI-144), which is where GCLI-144's marker already lives. Any CREATED in-repo edge on the five pins comes to opum-doc before the PR; removed edges are listed with it. Not started; the leader briefs it, ordering per opum-doc.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The bound and constraint forms (type A[T: x.run()], type A[T: (x.run(), int)]) with a later class-body import of x assert toEqual(REFUSED) and no C.run edge: red on origin/dev, green after, each measured by running both; module-level and no-class-binding twins keep their edges
A differential run, dev vs head, over a corpus of bound and constraint aliases: every head edge is also a dev edge; any created edge or bin gain comes to opum-doc before the PR
A mutant that drops the bound walk in the lazy scope turns the fixtures red; two review rounds at most (DEC-161)

implementationNotes: SCHEDULING (opum-doc, DEC-303 (a74) item 3, relayed by the leader 2026-11-27): the alias-bound wrong edge (the bound form type A[T: x.run()] and the constraint-tuple form type A[T: (x.run(), int)]) joins the (a49) item 7 hold list as a wrong-edge fix. Order: right after GCLI-144 and before GCLI-140 (the (a25) attribute-write rule); the (a36) item 8 pre-registration, GCLI-143, waits for it. It stays hold until the leader starts it. Two review rounds (DEC-161). Removal-only is proved by the same subset check as GCLI-144: every head edge is also a dev edge over the five pins, the fixtures and a differential corpus; any created edge or bin gain comes to opum-doc before the PR. GCLI-145 keeps the def and class bounds as an ordinary follow-up, not a hold.
